questions.text:
Consider the following recurrence:
[latex]T(n)=2T\left ( \sqrt{n}\right )+1, T(1)=1[/latex]
Which one of the following is true?
questions.solution:
Let [latex]n=2^m[/latex], [latex]S(m)=T(2^m)[/latex]: [latex]S(m)=2S(m/2)+1\Rightarrow S(m)=\Theta(m)[/latex].

So [latex]T(n)=\Theta(m)=\Theta(\log n)[/latex].

Answer: [latex]\Theta(\log n)[/latex]

questions.text: Algorithm design technique used in quicksort algorithm is?
questions.solution:
Quicksort partitions the array around a pivot (divide), sorts the two parts recursively (conquer), and needs no combine step: divide and conquer.

Answer: Divide and conquer

questions.text: In an adjacency list representation of an undirected simple graph G = (V,E), each edge (u,v) has two adjacency list entries: [v] in the adjacency list of u, and [u] in the adjacency list of v. These are called twins of each other. A twin pointer is a pointer from an adjacency list entry to its twin. If |E|=m and |V|=n, and the memory size is not a constraint, what is the Asymptotic Notation of the most efficient algorithm to set the twin pointer in each entry in each adjacency list?
questions.solution:
Go through all edges once (scanning every adjacency list), using an n [latex]\times[/latex] n table (memory is no problem) to remember where entry [v] in u's list is. When you meet [u] in v's list, look up its twin and link them. Each of the 2m entries is handled once, plus [latex]O(n)[/latex] to scan the lists.

Answer: [latex]\Theta(n+m)[/latex]

questions.text: The given diagram shows the flowchart for a recursive function A(n). Assume that all statements, except for the recursive calls,have O(1) Asymptotic Notation. If the worst case Asymptotic Notation of this functionis [latex]O(n^{\alpha })[/latex], then the least possible value(accurate upto two decimal positions) of [latex]\alpha[/latex] is .
questions.solution:
Worst-case path in the flowchart: A(n/2) at the start, then the right branch with two calls, then down with one more call, then the left branch with one more call. That is 5 calls to A(n/2).

[latex]T(n)=5T(n/2)+O(1)\Rightarrow T(n)=O(n^{\log_2 5})=O(n^{2.32})[/latex]

Answer: 2.32

questions.text: Let A1,A2,A3, and A4 be four matrices of dimensions 10x5, 5x20, 20x10, and 10x5, respectively. The minimum number of scalar multiplications required to find the product A1A2A3A4 using the basic matrix multiplication method is __________.
questions.solution:
Dimensions 10, 5, 20, 10, 5. Matrix chain DP:
- Pairs: A1A2 = 1000, A2A3 = 1000, A3A4 = 1000
- A2A3A4: (A2A3)A4 = 1000 + 5[latex]\cdot[/latex]10[latex]\cdot[/latex]5 = 1250
- A1A2A3A4: A1((A2A3)A4) = 1250 + 10[latex]\cdot[/latex]5[latex]\cdot[/latex]5 = 1500 (other splits give 3000 and 2000)

Answer: 1500
